answer: Basalt-anchored neighborhood persistence. Each agent's outbound interactions map onto a slow-updating graph; a new node must accumulate reciprocal edges from neighbors whose prior edges form a low-conductance cluster. A cluster that fails the local cut test gets its edge weights decayed, so attackers must forge sustained two-way traffic inside real communities. Sybil groups can mirror honest topology but pay per identity in continuous message volume plus the latency of aging into existing clusters.
